newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil fiscal imbalance a threat -- industry group.
newsitem.headline: Brazil fiscal imbalance a threat -- industry group.

text.p: Brazil's private National Industry Confederation (CNI) warned Tuesday that the fiscal deficit was the main threat to economic stability.

The group said in its monthly report that a recent decision by the Supreme Federal Tribunal, the country's highest court, to grant 11 civil servants a 28.9 percent wage rise would pressure the government's accounts over the long term.
"The imbalance in the public accounts is at the moment the main threat to the consolidation of economic stability," it said.

The report noted that a slight improvement in the public sector operational deficit last year, which reached 3.89 percent of gross domestic product after nearly 5.0 percent in 1995, was only "modest".
It noted that the primary result, which does not include debt servicing costs, actually worsened to a deficit of 0.09 percent of GDP from a slight surplus of 0.35 percent of GDP the year before.

"In addition, the report notes that the decision of the (court) implies a permanent increase in the federal government's payroll costs, which will have to be financed by higher taxes or cuts in other costs," it said.
The high court ruled last month in favour of 11 public sector workers who claimed they were entitled to a 28.9 percent wage increase awarded to army officers in 1993.

The government says it has not calculated what it would cost if the the ruling were extended to the rest of the public workforce, but independent analysts estimate a $5.0 billion a year hit, and up to $20 billion in backdated pay.
"In the face of this, (we) stress the need for energetic action by the government on the fiscal front in order to obtain in 1997 a significant reduction in the operational deficit," the CNI said.
The group said it considered fiscal cost-cutting measures "clearly superior" to monetarist steps to control demand, which would lead to greater insolvency.
